The normal Prothrombin Time and Alpha-Fetoprotein levels rule out acute liver failure and hepatocellular carcinoma, respectively. Given your history of rapid breathing, liver enlargement, and pitting edema without infection or structural defects, do you have a history of heart murmurs, shortness of breath with exertion, or bluish discoloration of your lips or fingers?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram: Presence of an atrial septal defect with left to right shunt

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congestive Heart Failure secondary to an Atrial Septal Defect. The combination of tachypnea (rapid breathing), hepatomegaly (liver enlargement), and pitting edema, confirmed by the echocardiogram showing a left-to-right shunt, indicates systemic venous congestion due to heart failure.
